```{python}
import numpyro

numpyro.set_host_device_count(4)

from numpyro import distributions as dist
from numpyro.infer import MCMC, NUTS

# Claude generated - get station information
import polars as pl

stations = (
    pl.read_csv("./ghcnd-stations.txt", has_header=False, separator="\x01",
                quote_char=None, new_columns=["raw"])
    .select(
        pl.col("raw").str.slice(0, 11).str.strip_chars().alias("ID"),
        pl.col("raw").str.slice(12, 8).str.strip_chars().cast(pl.Float64).alias("LAT"),
        pl.col("raw").str.slice(21, 9).str.strip_chars().cast(pl.Float64).alias("LON"),
        pl.col("raw").str.slice(31, 6).str.strip_chars().cast(pl.Float64).alias("ELEV"),
        pl.col("raw").str.slice(38, 2).str.strip_chars().alias("STATE"),
        pl.col("raw").str.slice(41, 30).str.strip_chars().alias("NAME"),
    )
)
```

```{python}
# Claude generated - load all MI station precipitation files
# Some stations have an all-null flag column (M_FLAG/Q_FLAG/OBS_TIME), which
# pyarrow infers as type Null instead of String, so a plain glob read fails
# with a schema mismatch. Cast those columns before concatenating.
import glob

files = sorted(glob.glob("mi_parquet/*.parquet"))
precip = pl.concat(
    [
        pl.read_parquet(f).with_columns(
            pl.col(["M_FLAG", "Q_FLAG", "S_FLAG", "OBS_TIME"]).cast(pl.Utf8),
            pl.col("DATE").str.strptime(pl.Date, "%Y%m%d")
        )
        for f in files
    ],
    how="vertical",
).join(stations, on="ID", how="left").select(
    pl.col("ID"), pl.col("LAT"), pl.col("LON"), pl.col("NAME"),
    pl.col("DATE"), pl.col("DATA_VALUE").alias("PRCP"),
).sort(["ID", "DATE"])
precip
```

```{python}
# numpyro has no built-in GEV, so we implement it as a custom Distribution.
# Block maxima converge (Fisher-Tippett-Gnedenko) to a GEV 
# Standard parameterization (loc, scale, concentration=xi):
#   z = (x - loc) / scale
#   xi != 0: logpdf = -log(scale) - (1 + 1/xi) * log1p(xi*z) - (1 + xi*z)^(-1/xi)
#            support: 1 + xi*z > 0
#   xi == 0 (Gumbel limit): logpdf = -log(scale) - z - exp(-z)
# Verified numerically against scipy.stats.genextreme(c=-xi, loc, scale).

import jax
import numpyro
from jax import numpy as jnp
from jax import random, lax
from numpyro import distributions as dist
from numpyro.distributions import constraints
from numpyro.distributions.util import promote_shapes, validate_sample
from numpyro.infer import MCMC, NUTS
import arviz as az

# Claude generated - implementation of GEV distribution in Numpyro
class GEV(dist.Distribution):
    arg_constraints = {
        "loc": constraints.real,
        "scale": constraints.positive,
        "concentration": constraints.real,
    }
    support = constraints.real
    reparametrized_params = ["loc", "scale", "concentration"]

    def __init__(self, loc, scale, concentration, validate_args=None):
        self.loc, self.scale, self.concentration = promote_shapes(loc, scale, concentration)
        batch_shape = lax.broadcast_shapes(jnp.shape(loc), jnp.shape(scale), jnp.shape(concentration))
        super().__init__(batch_shape=batch_shape, validate_args=validate_args)

    def sample(self, key, sample_shape=()):
        shape = sample_shape + self.batch_shape
        u = random.uniform(key, shape=shape)
        xi = self.concentration
        near0 = jnp.abs(xi) < 1e-6
        safe_xi = jnp.where(near0, 1.0, xi)
        z_gumbel = -jnp.log(-jnp.log(u))
        z_frechet = (jnp.power(-jnp.log(u), -safe_xi) - 1) / safe_xi
        z = jnp.where(near0, z_gumbel, z_frechet)
        return self.loc + self.scale * z

    @validate_sample
    def log_prob(self, value):
        xi = self.concentration
        z = (value - self.loc) / self.scale
        near0 = jnp.abs(xi) < 1e-6
        safe_xi = jnp.where(near0, 1.0, xi)
        u = 1 + safe_xi * z
        valid = jnp.where(near0, True, u > 0)
        safe_u = jnp.where(valid, u, 1.0)

        logp_gumbel = -jnp.log(self.scale) - z - jnp.exp(-z)
        logp_frechet = (
            -jnp.log(self.scale)
            - (1 + 1 / safe_xi) * jnp.log(safe_u)
            - jnp.power(safe_u, -1 / safe_xi)
        )
        logp = jnp.where(near0, logp_gumbel, logp_frechet)
        return jnp.where(valid, logp, -jnp.inf)
```

```{python}
# Build a "long format" dataset across all stations: one flat vector of
# observations (y_all) plus a parallel integer vector (station_idx) saying
# which station each observation belongs to. Advanced indexing
# (loc[station_idx]) then broadcasts each station's parameter out to
# exactly its own observations
min_years = 15
counts = yearly_max.group_by("ID").len().filter(pl.col("len") >= min_years)
station_ids_h = sorted(counts["ID"].to_list())
id_to_idx = {sid: i for i, sid in enumerate(station_ids_h)}
n_stations = len(station_ids_h)

ym = yearly_max.filter(pl.col("ID").is_in(station_ids_h)).sort(["ID", "year"])
station_idx = jnp.array([id_to_idx[sid] for sid in ym["ID"].to_list()])
y_all = jnp.array(ym["PRCP_MAX"].to_numpy())

print(f"{n_stations} stations, {y_all.shape[0]} station-years total")
```

```{python}
n_stations = len(jnp.unique(station_idx))

# lat/lon are station-level covariates (constant within a station), so build
# one value per station -- aligned to station_ids_h order, same as xi_raw's
# "stations" plate -- rather than repeating a row per station-year.
station_latlon = (
    ym
    .group_by("ID")
    .agg(
        pl.col("LAT").first().alias("LAT"),
        pl.col("LON").first().alias("LON"),
        pl.col("NAME").first().alias("NAME"),
    )
    .sort("ID")
)
assert station_latlon["ID"].to_list() == station_ids_h
# Standardize the covariates (not the response) -- this only rescales the
# design matrix and doesn't touch y, so it's not the prior-peeking concern
# from before; it just keeps lat_beta/lon_beta on a sane numeric scale.
lat_by_station = jnp.array(station_latlon["LAT"].to_numpy())
lon_by_station = jnp.array(station_latlon["LON"].to_numpy())
lat_z = (lat_by_station - lat_by_station.mean()) / lat_by_station.std()
lon_z = (lon_by_station - lon_by_station.mean()) / lon_by_station.std()

```

```{python}
def model(n_stations, station_idx, lat, lon, y):
    # loc is a single constant shared statewide.
    loc = numpyro.sample("loc", dist.Normal(300.0, 300.0))

    # scale carries the lat/lon spatial trend (in log-space, to keep it
    # positive) -- this is the classical "index-flood" regional-frequency-
    # analysis convention: location/scale are the well-estimated parameters
    # that carry spatial variation, while the shape parameter is treated as
    # roughly constant across a climatically homogeneous region, since xi
    # needs far more data to pin down than loc/scale do (this is exactly the
    # weak-identification problem we saw when xi carried the lat/lon trend).

    lat_lon_sigma = numpyro.sample("lat_long_sigma", dist.InverseGamma(1, 1))
    log_scale0 = numpyro.sample("log_scale0", dist.Normal(jnp.log(200.0), 1.0))
    scale_lat_beta = numpyro.sample("scale_lat_beta", dist.Normal(0.0, lat_lon_sigma))
    scale_lon_beta = numpyro.sample("scale_lon_beta", dist.Normal(0.0, lat_lon_sigma))
    tau_log_scale = numpyro.sample("tau_log_scale", dist.HalfNormal(0.3))

    log_scale_mean = (
        log_scale0 + scale_lat_beta * lat + scale_lon_beta * lon
    )  # length n_stations
    with numpyro.plate("stations", n_stations):
        log_scale_raw = numpyro.sample("log_scale_raw", dist.Normal(0.0, 1.0))
        xi_raw = numpyro.sample("xi_raw", dist.Normal(0.0, 1.0))
    scale = numpyro.deterministic(
        "scale", jnp.exp(log_scale_mean + tau_log_scale * log_scale_raw)
    )

    # xi stays a single pooled hierarchical parameter -- no spatial trend.
    mu_xi = numpyro.sample("mu_xi", dist.Normal(0.0, 0.2))
    tau_xi = numpyro.sample("tau_xi", dist.HalfNormal(0.15))
    xi = numpyro.deterministic("xi", mu_xi + tau_xi * xi_raw)

    with numpyro.plate("obs", y.shape[0]):
        numpyro.sample("y_obs", GEV(loc, scale[station_idx], xi[station_idx]), obs=y)


kernel = NUTS(model, init_strategy=numpyro.infer.init_to_median(num_samples=50))
mcmc = MCMC(kernel, num_warmup=2000, num_samples=4000, num_chains=4)
mcmc.run(
    jax.random.key(23),
    station_idx=station_idx,
    y=y_all,
    lat=lat_z,
    lon=lon_z,
    n_stations=n_stations,
)
```

```{python}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.stats import genpareto, genextreme
from scipy.optimize import minimize
from scipy.special import gamma
from pathlib import Path
import lmoments3 as lmom

def fit_gev(x):
    """
    Fit a generalized extreme value distribution (GEV) using maximum likelihood
    estimation to the data in 'x'. Probability weighted moments are used to obtain
    starting values:
    https://www.stat.cmu.edu/technometrics/80-89/VOL-27-03/v2703251.pdf

    The returned frozen GEV distribution follows the scipy parameterization:

    https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.genextreme.html

    Note that this differs from another common parameterization, which is the one
    used on Wikipedia:

    https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generalized_extreme_value_distribution
    """

    x = np.sort(x)
    n = len(x)

    # Plotting positions
    pp = np.arange(1 / 2, n + 1 / 2) / n

    # Calculate the first three probability weighted moments
    b = np.zeros(3)
    for r in range(3):
        b[r] = np.dot(pp**r, x) / n

    # The PWM estimator of Hoskins et al.
    c = (2 * b[1] - b[0]) / (3 * b[2] - b[0]) - np.log(2) / np.log(3)
    shape = 7.8590 * c + 2.9554 * c**2
    scale = (2 * b[1] - b[0]) * shape / (gamma(1 + shape) * (1 - 1 / 2**shape))
    loc = b[0] + scale * (gamma(1 + shape) - 1) / shape
    ge = genextreme(shape, loc=loc, scale=scale)

    # Get the MLE
    def f(par):
        shape, loc, logscale = par
        d = genextreme(shape, loc=loc, scale=np.exp(logscale))
        return -d.logpdf(x).sum()

    logscale = np.log(scale)
    x0 = np.asarray([shape, loc, logscale])
    rr = minimize(f, x0, method="powell")
    shape, loc, logscale = rr.x
    ge = genextreme(shape, loc=loc, scale=np.exp(logscale))
    return ge


gev_ests = {
    station[0]: fit_gev(sub_df["PRCP_MAX"])
    for station, sub_df in ym.group_by("ID")
}
```

Shrinkage estimator.

```{python}
# Compare the hierarchical posterior estimate of each station's tail index
# to its single-station MLE (from gev_ests). scipy's genextreme shape `c`
# is the negative of the standard EVT tail index xi (see the note in
# fit_gev), so flip its sign.
mle_xi = np.array([-gev_ests[sid].args[0] for sid in station_ids_h])

xi_da = trace.posterior["xi"]  # dims: chain, draw, station (in station_ids_h order)
post_xi_mean = xi_da.mean(dim=("chain", "draw")).values
post_xi_lo = xi_da.quantile(0.025, dim=("chain", "draw")).values
post_xi_hi = xi_da.quantile(0.975, dim=("chain", "draw")).values

plt.clf()
ax = plt.axes()
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.5)
lo, hi = min(mle_xi.min(), post_xi_lo.min()), max(mle_xi.max(), post_xi_hi.max())
ax.plot([lo, hi], [lo, hi], "--", color="gray", label="y = x (no shrinkage)")
ax.errorbar(
    mle_xi, post_xi_mean,
    yerr=[post_xi_mean - post_xi_lo, post_xi_hi - post_xi_mean],
    fmt="o", alpha=0.6, capsize=2,
)
mu_xi_da = trace.posterior["mu_xi"]
mu_xi_mean = mu_xi_da.mean().item()
mu_xi_lo = mu_xi_da.quantile(0.025).item()
mu_xi_hi = mu_xi_da.quantile(0.975).item()
ax.axhspan(mu_xi_lo, mu_xi_hi, color="orange", alpha=0.15, label="pooled mean ($\\xi$), 95% CI")
ax.axhline(mu_xi_mean, color="orange", ls=":")
ax.set_xlabel("MLE tail index ($\\hat\\xi_i$)")
ax.set_ylabel("Hierarchical posterior tail index ($\\tilde\\xi_i$)")
ax.set_title("Tail-Index Shrinkage")
ax.legend()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
# 100-year daily-precipitation return level across Michigan: the GEV quantile
# z_T solving F(z_T) = 1 - 1/T. This uses posterior-MEAN loc/scale/xi as a
# point-estimate ("plug-in") surface for a clean map -- not a full posterior
# average of the return level over all draws, which would differ slightly by
# Jensen's inequality since z_T is a nonlinear function of xi. Good enough
# for a point map; a full posterior version would show a spread per pixel.
def gev_return_level(loc, scale, xi, T):
    p = 1.0 / T
    return loc + scale / xi * ((-np.log1p(-p)) ** (-xi) - 1.0)

T = 100  # corresponds to once in 100 year storms
loc_mean = trace.posterior["loc"].mean().item()
log_scale0_mean = trace.posterior["log_scale0"].mean().item()
scale_lat_beta_mean = trace.posterior["scale_lat_beta"].mean().item()
scale_lon_beta_mean = trace.posterior["scale_lon_beta"].mean().item()
mu_xi_mean = trace.posterior["mu_xi"].mean().item()

# Grid prediction uses only the systematic lat/lon trend (mu_xi for xi, since
# xi has no spatial trend) -- it deliberately excludes each station's own
# idiosyncratic residual (tau_log_scale * log_scale_raw), which wouldn't
# generalize to an arbitrary new location.
grid_lon, grid_lat = np.meshgrid(
    np.linspace(lon_min, lon_max, 200),
    np.linspace(lat_min, lat_max, 200),
)
grid_lat_z = (grid_lat - lat_by_station.mean()) / lat_by_station.std()
grid_lon_z = (grid_lon - lon_by_station.mean()) / lon_by_station.std()
# scale prediction is the only thing geographic
scale_surface = np.exp(log_scale0_mean + scale_lat_beta_mean * grid_lat_z + scale_lon_beta_mean * grid_lon_z)
return_level_surface = gev_return_level(loc_mean, scale_surface, mu_xi_mean, T)

# Station overlay uses each station's own fitted scale/xi (including its
# partial-pooling residual), so it can be compared honestly to the trend.
post_scale_by_station = trace.posterior["scale"].mean(dim=("chain", "draw")).values
post_xi_by_station = trace.posterior["xi"].mean(dim=("chain", "draw")).values
return_level_by_station = gev_return_level(loc_mean, post_scale_by_station, post_xi_by_station, T)

# Data are in tenths of mm; 1 tenth-mm = 0.01 cm.
return_level_surface_cm = return_level_surface * 0.01
return_level_by_station_cm = return_level_by_station * 0.01

# Mask the grid to Michigan's actual land polygon (both peninsulas), not
# just the rectangular lat/lon bounding box, so only the state is colored.
import shapely
import cartopy.io.shapereader as shpreader
shp = shpreader.natural_earth(resolution="10m", category="cultural", name="admin_1_states_provinces_lakes")
michigan_geom = next(
    rec.geometry for rec in shpreader.Reader(shp).records() if rec.attributes.get("name") == "Michigan"
)
in_michigan = shapely.contains_xy(michigan_geom, grid_lon, grid_lat)
return_level_surface_cm = np.where(in_michigan, return_level_surface_cm, np.nan)

vmin = np.floor(np.nanmin(return_level_surface_cm) * 10) / 10
vmax = np.ceil(np.nanmax(return_level_surface_cm) * 10) / 10

fig = plt.figure(figsize=(7, 8))
ax = plt.axes(projection=ccrs.PlateCarree())
ax.set_extent([lon_min, lon_max, lat_min, lat_max], crs=ccrs.PlateCarree())

cf = ax.contourf(
    grid_lon, grid_lat, return_level_surface_cm, levels=21, cmap="YlOrRd",
    vmin=vmin, vmax=vmax, transform=ccrs.PlateCarree(), zorder=1,
)
ax.add_feature(cfeature.LAKES.with_scale("10m"), facecolor="white", zorder=2)
ax.add_feature(cfeature.OCEAN.with_scale("10m"), facecolor="white", zorder=2)
ax.coastlines(resolution="10m", linewidth=0.7, zorder=3)
ax.add_feature(cfeature.STATES.with_scale("10m"), linewidth=0.5, zorder=3)
ax.add_feature(cfeature.BORDERS.with_scale("10m"), linewidth=0.5, zorder=3)

ax.scatter(
    station_latlon["LON"], station_latlon["LAT"],
    c=return_level_by_station_cm, cmap="YlOrRd", vmin=vmin, vmax=vmax,
    edgecolor="black", linewidth=0.6, s=40,
    transform=ccrs.PlateCarree(), zorder=4,
)

cbar = plt.colorbar(cf, ax=ax, shrink=0.7, label=f"{T}-year daily precipitation (cm)")
cbar.ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(lambda x, pos: f"{x:.1f}")
plt.title(f"Posterior mean of {T}-year storm size")
plt.show()
```

```{python}
# Station-level 100-year return level with credible intervals, ordered by
# posterior mean -- the numeric complement to the map, showing each
# station's own estimate and uncertainty explicitly instead of as a color.
rl_samples = gev_return_level(
    trace.posterior["loc"], trace.posterior["scale"], trace.posterior["xi"], T
) * 0.01  # cm

rl_mean = rl_samples.mean(dim=("chain", "draw"))
rl_lo = rl_samples.quantile(0.025, dim=("chain", "draw"))
rl_hi = rl_samples.quantile(0.975, dim=("chain", "draw"))

order = np.argsort(rl_mean.values)
labels_sorted = rl_mean["station"].values[order]
mean_sorted = rl_mean.values[order]
lo_sorted = rl_lo.values[order]
hi_sorted = rl_hi.values[order]
y_pos = np.arange(len(labels_sorted))

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 10))
ax.errorbar(
    mean_sorted, y_pos,
    xerr=[mean_sorted - lo_sorted, hi_sorted - mean_sorted],
    fmt="o", color="firebrick", ecolor="black", capsize=3, markersize=4,
)
ax.set_yticks(y_pos)
ax.set_yticklabels(labels_sorted, fontsize=9)
ax.set_ylim(-1, len(labels_sorted))
ax.set_xlabel(f"{T}-year daily precipitation return level (cm)")
ax.set_title(f"Station-level {T}-year return level, ordered\n(posterior mean, 95% credible interval)")
ax.grid(True, axis="x", alpha=0.4)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
# Both diagnostics (MLE QQ and hierarchical posterior predictive check) for
# both a small-record and a large-record station, so the two methods can be
# compared directly at each end of the sample-size range.
# small_id: fewest years in the fitted set. large_id: most years.
small_id = "USW00054854"  # Gaylord 9 SSW, 19 years
large_id = "USW00014824"  # Escanaba, 142 years

loc_draws = trace.posterior["loc"].values.flatten()


def mle_qq(station_id):
    y = np.sort(ym.filter(pl.col("ID") == station_id)["PRCP_MAX"].to_numpy())
    n = len(y)
    pp = np.arange(1, n + 1) / (n + 1)
    q_cm = gev_ests[station_id].ppf(pp) * 0.01
    return y * 0.01, q_cm


def bayes_ppc(station_id):
    # Simulates a full replicate n-year record from EVERY posterior draw and
    # uses the spread of simulated order statistics as the band, so it
    # captures both parameter uncertainty and finite-sample order-statistic
    # variability (a naive "quantile function + parameter uncertainty" band
    # undercovers, as found earlier for Ann Arbor).
    idx = id_to_idx[station_id]
    y = np.sort(ym.filter(pl.col("ID") == station_id)["PRCP_MAX"].to_numpy())
    n = len(y)
    scale_draws = trace.posterior["scale"].values[:, :, idx].flatten()
    xi_draws = trace.posterior["xi"].values[:, :, idx].flatten()
    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
    u = rng.uniform(size=(loc_draws.shape[0], n))
    xi_b = xi_draws[:, None]
    z = ((-np.log(u)) ** (-xi_b) - 1.0) / xi_b
    sim_sorted = np.sort(loc_draws[:, None] + scale_draws[:, None] * z, axis=1)
    med_cm = np.median(sim_sorted, axis=0) * 0.01
    lo_cm = np.quantile(sim_sorted, 0.05, axis=0) * 0.01
    hi_cm = np.quantile(sim_sorted, 0.95, axis=0) * 0.01
    return y * 0.01, med_cm, lo_cm, hi_cm


fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 5.5))

for ax, (sid, label) in zip(axes, [(small_id, "Gaylord 9 SSW"), (large_id, "Escanaba")]):
    y_cm, mle_q_cm = mle_qq(sid)
    y_cm2, med, plo, phi = bayes_ppc(sid)

    lo = min(mle_q_cm.min(), y_cm.min(), plo.min(), y_cm2.min())
    hi = max(mle_q_cm.max(), y_cm.max(), phi.max(), y_cm2.max())
    ax.plot([lo, hi], [lo, hi], "--", color="gray", zorder=0)

    ax.scatter(mle_q_cm, y_cm, color="darkorange", alpha=0.75, s=50, label="MLE")
    ax.errorbar(
        med, y_cm2, xerr=[med - plo, phi - med],
        fmt="o", color="teal", ecolor="lightseagreen", alpha=0.75, capsize=2,
        label="Hierarchical posterior",
    )

    ax.set_xlabel("Model-fitted GEV quantile (cm)")
    ax.set_ylabel("Observed annual max (cm)")
    ax.set_title(f"{label} (n={len(y_cm)})")
    ax.grid(True, alpha=0.4)
    ax.legend()

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
# Directional evidence for the lat/lon effect on scale, reported as a
# posterior probability rather than "does the credible interval exclude
# zero" -- P(beta < 0 | data) is a direct, honest Bayesian statement and
# needs no correction for repeated testing the way a frequentist p-value
# comparison would.
p_lat_neg = (trace.posterior["scale_lat_beta"] < 0).mean().item()
p_lon_neg = (trace.posterior["scale_lon_beta"] < 0).mean().item()
print(f"P(scale_lat_beta < 0 | data) = {p_lat_neg:.3f}")
print(f"P(scale_lon_beta < 0 | data) = {p_lon_neg:.3f}")
```

```{python}
# Compare within-station uncertainty (each station's own 95% credible
# interval for its return level) to the across-station geographic spread
# (range of point estimates across the state). If per-station CI widths are
# comparable to or larger than the geographic spread, that's the
# quantitative version of "the lat/lon effect isn't practically meaningful."
rl_samples_cm = gev_return_level(
    trace.posterior["loc"], trace.posterior["scale"], trace.posterior["xi"], T
) * 0.01
rl_lo_by_station = rl_samples_cm.quantile(0.025, dim=("chain", "draw")).values
rl_hi_by_station = rl_samples_cm.quantile(0.975, dim=("chain", "draw")).values
ci_width_by_station = rl_hi_by_station - rl_lo_by_station

state_spread = return_level_by_station_cm.max() - return_level_by_station_cm.min()

print(f"Per-station 95% CI width (cm): mean={ci_width_by_station.mean():.2f}, "
      f"median={np.median(ci_width_by_station):.2f}, "
      f"range=[{ci_width_by_station.min():.2f}, {ci_width_by_station.max():.2f}]")
print(f"Spread of point estimates across all stations (max - min): {state_spread:.2f} cm")
```
